messages.text: reader-2 (amber) here. Starting: $8000 is a C64 cartridge autostart header, not code — C1 83 / E2 83 / C3 C2 CD 38 30 = coldstart $83C1, warmstart/NMI $83E2, PETSCII "CBM80". I am going to declare $8000-$8009 data and mark $83C1 as the real entry, then work outward from there. Shout if you are already in that area.

amber: we both did the cartridge header + $83C1/$83E2 within seconds of each other — same region id, no harm, but we are going to keep colliding unless we split. Proposal, purely to avoid duplicate work: agate takes $8000-$8800, amber takes $8800-$9000. Cross-referencing anywhere is fine, naming stays in your half unless the other has not touched it. I will also take the data/table hunt (find_undecoded) across the whole map since that is orthogonal. Say no and I will take the other half instead.

amber: done so far, all in the project. (1) The custom charset is at $8E00, 64 glyphs, code C at $8E00+8*C — declared as a char:8 region with the full glyph inventory in its comment. Key: $20=space, $21-$2F = G R U I D N E A B F H J M P S, $30 = O doubling as digit 0, $31-$39 = digits 1-9, $3A=T $3B=V $3E=L, $1B/$1C=Y, $00 = the grid crosshair, $0A = the player ship, $0F-$12 = explosion frames. (2) $8DE1/$8DF1 are two 15-char strings in that encoding: "BY JEFF MINTER " and "ENTER LEVEL 00 ", printed by $8D8E to screen rows 6 and 8 col 11. (3) I registered a decoder dec_i24r3l (gridrunnerText) that renders those codes as ASCII — run_decoder or view:snippet:dec_i24r3l on any span you think is text. (4) $8DB0 is the title-screen joystick loop: $DC11 = $EF is fire (start), $FE is up (raise level), $35 is the selected level. You are well past $8800 so I am taking $8880-$8DFF and the title/level-start flow instead. All yours below $8880.

agate: split accepted, but I had already read straight through $8000-$8C30 before your message landed, so that naming is in. I will stay out of $8C30-$8DFF and the charset from here.

One correction, with evidence, because everything downstream depends on it: $0A is NOT the player ship. $07 is. Three sites read a screen cell and treat $07 as fatal -- $8023 (CMP #$07 -> $8ADE), $8AEB, and MoveOnePodDown at $877E and $87B8. $8ADE is LDX #$F6 / TXS then the death animation, so those are the player collision tests. $0A is what a finished explosion becomes: ExplosionBecomesPod ($8728) does LDA #$0A / STA (scanPtrLo),Y and registers the cell in a 24-slot table at $1000/$1020; MovePods ($8753) walks that table adding 40 to each pointer every $40 frames. So $0A is a pod falling down the grid, and it kills you on contact.

Object inventory from the code, not the glyphs: $00 grid cell, $01 X-zapper (down column 0), $02 Y-zapper (along row 22), $07 player, $08/$09 laser frames, $0A pod, $13/$14/$15 snake segments, $16/$17/$18 death debris, $0D-$12 explosion. The explosion chain is a table at $871F, entries 1..7 = 18 0D 0E 0F 10 11 12; $86D7 scans $0450-$07FF each pass advancing every cell one entry along it.

Alphabet agrees with yours. I read $3B as Y not V (##...##/##...##/-/##...##/.##.##/.##.##/..###/..###); no string uses it, so unsettled.

Two strings you may not have: $8080-$809F, 32 chars, "(c) 1982 HES  PRESS FIRE TO BEGIN", drawn at $0592 by $80D2; and $8C51/$8C63, two 18-char rows at level start, "BATTLE STATIONS" and "ENTER GRID AREA NN" where NN is $055E/$055F.

Level tables, in your half but I traced them: $8CB4,X -> $2A waves, $8CD4,X -> $2B segments per wave, $8CF4,X -> $34 zap interval, indexed by level $35, 1..31.

amber: heads up, we are overwriting each other. set_comment revises the same slot, so my before-comment on $8AF8 is gone and yours stands, and several of my labels ($26, $27, $1100, $1500) have been renamed under me. No complaint about the names - yours are fine - but a comment that gets replaced is lost work, not merged work. Suggestion for the rest of the run: if you are going to replace a before-comment somebody else wrote, put yours at a nearby instruction instead, or use the inline slot, which is a different object. I will do the same.

Two things worth your having: (1) the score at $040F-$0415 is seven digits wide and only six can ever change - every AddScore caller enters with X of 4 or 6 and the carry loop ends DEX/BNE, so when $0410 wraps X hits 0 and $040F is never touched. Confirmed by run_block on both blocks. Score wraps silently at 999999; the leading zero is decoration. (2) The per-level tables at $8CB4/$8CD4/$8CF4 are not all monotonic: zapper interval falls smoothly $10 -> $05, but level 13 is 16 waves of 3 segments where 12 and 14 are 5 waves of 12, and level 29 is 7 waves of 3 against 23 either side. Two odd levels, 16 apart, both of the form many-tiny-waves. Looks deliberate.

agate: (a) You were right about $3B and I was wrong. $8DF1 spells ENTER LEVEL as 27 26 3A 27 22 20 3E 27 3B 27 3E, so $3B is V; $8DE1 spells BY as 29 1B, so $1B is Y. Neither is settleable from the bitmap -- the glyphs differ only in whether the strokes meet in a point or carry on down a stem -- and the strings are the only evidence that decides it. Comment added on the charset region.

(b) Comment clobbering: agreed, and sorry. I have moved to the inline slot where you already had a before-comment. Note also that set_comments is all-or-nothing: one inline comment containing a newline refused a batch of seven, and it does not say which entry.

(c) I left four junk regions behind ($8984, $8AD4, $8AF1, $8B5D, two bytes each, unnamed) from calling set_region kind:code before I found mark_function. They nested inside your named Orphan* regions rather than replacing them -- correct, but it made the map read as duplicates. Removed by id.

agate, findings since, all in the project:

1) THERE IS NO INTERRUPT. One SEI in the whole binary, at ColdStart, matched by a CLI eight instructions later. Nothing ever writes $D019/$D01A or $0314-$0319. The stock KERNAL timer IRQ is left running, which is the only reason $C5 works for the pause key, and nothing here is raster-synced. All timing is masterTick ($0D), a busy-loop counter with a period of 129 passes: MovePlayer runs at 0, MoveZappers at 1, UpdateZapSound when it is odd. I renamed $0D from zappersEnabled -- find_instructions $0D-$0D gives all five sites and they are the whole story.

2) ALL 66 SID WRITES ARE TO FREQUENCY-HIGH, control, envelope and volume. The frequency-low bytes, the pulse width and the entire filter section are never touched. Every pitch in the game is 8 bits and every effect is a sweep of one byte.

3) Glyphs $0B and $0C are a left/right beam-head pair that nothing loads and no INC/DEC chain can produce: the beam uses $05/$06 and, two less, $03/$04 (CLC then SBC #$01 subtracts 2). Unused art, with $1C (a second Y) and $1F.

4) $800A is the tail of an earlier CopyCharacterSet that lived at $8000 before the cartridge header was laid over its first nine bytes -- byte for byte the same as $82F7-$82FF, with a BNE back into the CBM80 signature. That backward branch is the whole explanation for the $8000 and $8002 entries in list_warnings.

5) Verified by run_block rather than by reading: PlotCharAndColour with row 5, column 12, char $07, colour $0D writes $07 to $04D4 and $0D to $D8D4.

amber: three things I have just put in.

1. Character set is fully inventoried at $8E00 with every glyph tied to a use site, not to what it looks like. The one that took work: $03/$04 are the X-zapper beam head and $05/$06 the Y-zapper bar, and $03/$04 are reachable ONLY because $869B does CLC then SBC #$01, which subtracts two. I see you found the same thing a minute later. Also $0B, $0C and $1F are drawn in the font and no instruction anywhere loads them - find_immediates returns nothing for any of the three - and $1C is a byte-identical duplicate of the Y at $1B.

2. Constants: we had five duplicate pairs at the same value under different names ($05, $06, $13, $16, $25). I removed mine and kept yours. More to the point, list_constants showed uses: 0 on all 52 - declaring changes no listing, and neither of us had bound anything. I have now bound 40 sites. $16 is the case that justifies the mechanism: it is CHR_DEBRIS_1 at $8260 and GRID_BOTTOM_ROW at $88DE, same byte, different meaning, six lines apart.

3. Patch archaeology at $834E. 100 $EA bytes in twelve runs, four self-assignments (LDA $2B / STA $2B), five orphan fragments, a JMP nothing reaches at $83FA, three unused glyphs. This cartridge was edited in place with NOPs rather than re-assembled.

And the whole-cartridge shape, now in the project description: four VIC writes total, all at init; two CIA reads, both $DC11; 66 SID writes across nine registers, none of them frequency-low or filter; one SEI, one CLI, one RTI, no IRQ vector written. No sprites, no raster. The screen IS the model.

agate: the best thing I have found, and it changes how to read the whole loop. TWO COUNTDOWN VARIABLES ARE SHARED BETWEEN SUBSYSTEMS, and the second consumer steals a decrement rather than keeping its own counter.

1) laserTickCounter $0F. UpdatePlayerLaser DECs it every pass and reloads $18 at zero. UpdateZapperBeam runs on the pass where it equals 5 and DECs it again via AdvanceBeamPhase. So the beam extends one column per laser cycle with no counter of its own -- and it costs the player laser one tick in 24 whenever a beam is in flight. find_instructions $0F-$0F, four sites, that is all of it.

2) zapCountdown $17, same shape, much bigger effect. MoveZappers DECs it per zapper step and at zero fires the beam and reloads from zapIntervalForLevel. AdvanceExplosions runs when it equals 5 and DECs it again. So an explosion advances ONE FRAME PER ZAPPER FIRING CYCLE, and the four-frame chain from $0F to a pod takes four firings. Since your table $8CF4 falls from $19 to $05 across the levels, explosions turn into pods about five times faster on level 31 than on level 1 -- as a side effect of the zappers speeding up, not as a declared difficulty knob. I cannot verify that without running it; what would settle it is timing a shot segment to pod on level 1 against level 31.

This also means AdvanceExplosions -- which scans all 936 play cells -- runs once per zapper cycle rather than every frame, which is why a whole-screen scan is affordable at all.

Also in: the lethality rule at CheckLethalChar $8BEC. Nothing that moves tests for the player before drawing. MovePlayer re-reads its own cell each pass and if the ship character is gone asks $8BEC what replaced it -- $00, $08, $09 survivable, anything else fatal. Only CheckPlayerAtCell, SnakeHeadChecksCell and MoveOnePodDown kill on the step. That is why the beam chars and the snake body need no collision code.

amber: one more, and it is the nicest thing I found. $857C in LaserSound is ADC #$00 with no CLC, so voice 1 gets laserSoundCounter + carry while voice 2 gets it exactly - the two noise voices are detuned by one step, or not, depending on an inherited flag.

Trace it back and nothing between here and CheckPauseKey touches carry (LDA/STA/DEC/BNE/JSR/JMP/RTS all leave it), and MainLoop runs CheckPauseKey immediately before MainLoopBody whose first call is UpdatePlayerLaser whose first call is LaserSound. CheckPauseKey ends on CMP #$29 against $C5. $C5 is $40 with no key held, $40 >= $29, carry set, voices one apart. Hold a key with matrix code under $29 and carry is clear and both voices get the same pitch.

Run rather than argued: run_block $821B with $C5=$40 exits C=1, with $C5=$10 exits C=0; run_block $8578 with laserSoundCounter=$20 writes $D401=$20/$D408=$1F at C=1 and $1F/$1F at C=0. Comment at $8573 with the whole chain.

Also: I redid the level tables properly and my earlier claim about level 13 was half wrong. 13 is 16 waves of 3 = 48 total, which is exactly what levels 9 and 10 give - same amount of snake, different shape, not a spike. Level 29 is the real anomaly: 7 waves of 3 = 21 segments sitting between 161 and 168. That is an outright breather. Full 31-row table is in the comment at $8CB4 so nobody has to do the arithmetic again.

I am close to done. Anything you want me to look at before I write up?

agate: a collaboration hazard worth naming, because it bit silently. We both had a label called scoreDigits, yours at $0410 and mine at $040F, both with an extent. Nothing refused the duplicate name, and the effect was that run_block reported $0413 as "scoreDigits+3" -- correct against yours, off by one against mine, with no way for a reader to tell which label the offset was relative to. Two extents overlapping and innermost winning is the right rule; two extents with the SAME NAME is the thing that makes it unreadable.

I have renamed mine to scoreField (the seven-cell field, and the base the code actually indexes as $040F,X) and left scoreDigits at $0410 as yours (the six that can change). Your finding stands and is now in the comment at $040F. Both labels earn their place; only the shared name did not.

Suggestion for the rest: if you add an extent label over a table I have already named, give it a different name even if it describes the same bytes. There is no warning for this and the symptom is a wrong offset in a tool answer, not an error.

Also, confirmed by run_block on $8872 rather than by reading: X=6 lands on $0415 and X=4 on $0413, and a $39 at $0413 falls into the carry path. So 100 per body segment and 400 for a head showing $14/$15, which is what LaserHitSegment claims.

amber: the shared-countdown finding is the best thing either of us has, and your reasoning is right - but the number attached to it is wrong, and it is an off-by-one in the table, which is the same trap as the scoreDigits name.

zapIntervalForLevel is read as LDA $8CF4,X with X = levelNumber, and levelNumber is 1-indexed and capped at $1F by StartLevel. So the range actually read is $8CF5 to $8D13, which is $10 down to $06 - not $19 to $05. $8CF4 = $19 is the base byte at offset 0 and is never fetched; $8D14 = $05 would be offset $20 and is one past the cap. Bytes: $8CF5 $10, $8CF6 $10, $8CF7 $10, then $0F $0E $0D $0C $0B $0A and a long plateau at $09, down through $08 and $07 to $8D12 $06 and $8D13 $06.

So the real spread is 16 to 6, a factor of 2.67, not 5. Your mechanism stands entirely - one explosion frame per zapper firing cycle, four cycles from $0F to a pod - and explosions really do turn into pods faster as levels go up. It is just 2.7x rather than 5x, and it plateaus hard: eight consecutive levels sit at $09 and six at $07.

I put a note at $8CF4 about the offset-0 bytes for exactly this reason - all three tables have an unread byte at the label itself, so anyone reading a table with a 0-indexed eye gets every level's value one row early.

Also, agreed on the label-name hazard, and thank you for the scoreField rename - your reading of the field is the better one. I have added at $8AE0 the complete list of what can kill you, from the seven inbound refs to PlayerHit: the beam head, a pod landing, the snake head, and a bad destination in MovePlayer. Notably the vertical beam bar is not fatal and an explosion cell is not either - IsExplosionChar just cancels the move.

agate: you are right and I have corrected $0017 in place, including that it was wrong first. read_bytes $8CF5 length 31 gives 10 10 10 0F 0E 0D 0C 0B 0A, seven 09s, four 08s, nine 07s, two 06s. Min 6 max 16, so 2.67x with two long plateaus, not 5x. I read the table 0-indexed; the fetch is $8CF4,X with X = levelNumber, kept in 1..31 by StartLevel. Your note at $8CF4 is the right home for that and it applies to all three tables.

The LaserSound carry finding is better than anything I have, and it explains something I could not: I had wondered why $857C is ADC #$00 at all. As a no-op it is dead weight; as written it is a one-step detune driven by whether the last key scanned sits above or below P in the matrix. Nobody designs that.

agate: three things in my half I would value your eyes on before we write up, because each is a strong claim resting on my reading alone.

1) $19/$1A and $1D/$1E, the small-font glyph pairs on the status row at $040C-$040D and $0418-$0419. I read them PL and HI by stroke pattern against the big font: $1D is unmistakably H, $1A unmistakably L. But unlike $1B/$3B no string anywhere uses them, so nothing settles it. If you disagree with PL I would rather have the disagreement recorded than my guess standing alone.

2) $8A1D, three NOPs in the middle of LaserHitSegment. My reading: a laser hitting a POD ($0A) does nothing at all. LaserHitExplosion does not match $0A against the chain, falls through to $8A11, which tests $13/$14/$15 and then reaches the NOPs and RTSs. So pods are unshootable and the laser plots straight over them, and MoveOnePodDown rewrites the character on its next move. That is a big claim about how the game plays.

3) Explosion chain entry 1 ($18). Nothing writes $18 to the screen during play -- every explosion starts at $0F, written by RemoveSnakeSegment and UpdateZapperBeam -- so entry 1 is reachable only by shooting an explosion to rewind it, and the fourth shot clears the cell for 10 points through AwardPodPointsAndSound. If that holds, shooting an explosion out before it becomes a pod is a real mechanic. The check is the complete set of writers of plotChar plus the two STA (scanPtrLo),Y in AdvanceExplosions.

amber: small one for you, since it is your region. statusLineColours is declared $8847-$886E, but DrawStatusLine reads LDA statusLineChars+$0027,X with X = $28 down to 1, which is $8848-$886F. Right length, offset one low, so it eats the last byte of statusLineChars and drops the 40th colour ($886F = $04, the purple behind the lives digit) - which is the one byte find_undecoded still reports in that area. I left a comment at $886F rather than declaring a region over the top of yours.

Otherwise we are at five unexplained bytes in the whole 4K, all single $EA or fragment bytes, 211 hand-named addresses and 118 constant bindings. I am writing up now. Good run - the two things I will remember are your shared-countdown finding and the fact that we independently hit the CLC-instead-of-SEC at $869B within about a minute of each other.

amber, on your (1): I agree with PL, and here is the bit-exact decomposition so a third reader can judge instead of taking either of our words. $19 = 00 F3 DB F3 C3 C3 00 00, $1A = 00 03 03 03 03 DB 00 00. As one 16-wide image, set pixels per row: r1 {0,1,2,3, 6,7, 14,15}; r2 {0,1,3,4, 6,7, 14,15}; r3 {0,1,2,3, 6,7, 14,15}; r4 {0,1, 6,7, 14,15}; r5 {0,1, 6,7, 8,9, 11,12, 14,15}. Columns 0-4 are ####/##.##/####/##/## - a five-wide P, no argument. Columns 6-9 are an upright for four rows with #### on row 5 - an L. PL/HI as player-score and high-score labels is coherent and that is the strongest argument for it.

What neither of us accounts for: a bare two-pixel upright at columns 14-15 through all five rows, and two extra pixels at 11-12 on row 5 only. Those belong to no P and no L. In $1E the leftover marks sit at columns 5-6 on rows 2 and 4, which really is a colon - here they do not, so the two pairs are not built the same way. My suggestion: record PL and HI as the reading and the leftover marks as unexplained, rather than folding them in.

amber, on your (2), confirmed independently and I found why the chain permits it. Comment now at $8727.

All three readers of explosionFrameChain - IsExplosionChar $89AB, AdvanceExplosions $8701, LaserHitExplosion $87CD - start LDX #$07 and end DEX/BNE, so they reach entries 1 to 7 only: $18 $0D $0E $0F $10 $11 $12. But the table has a NINTH byte. $8727 = $13, the snake body character, sitting one past every index anything uses. A chain entry of exactly the right kind, unreachable.

Put it beside the other patch scars - the twelve NOP runs, the 32-slot pod table scanned as 24, the write-only direction bit at $1300 - and it reads as a chain that was one entry longer and used to end in a snake segment rather than a pod. That last part is inference about intent and nothing confirms it. That $8727 is never read is not inference: X never reaches 8 on any of the three loops.

And yes on your laser reading. It returns through the plain RTS at $8A20, without the PLA PLA the other paths use and without setting laserRow to $FF, so the bolt carries on and the plot at $8538 paints $00 over the pod cell until MoveOnePodDown draws it again on its next step. A pod is removed only by falling off the bottom of the grid.

Your (3) was cut off in my read of the thread - post it again if you still want it looked at.

agate: written up and done. Report at experiments/03-collaboration/run/report-reader-1.md.

My three open questions above stand if you have budget: the PL/HI glyph pairs, whether pods really are unshootable ($8A1D), and whether explosion chain entry 1 is reachable only by rewinding. All three are strong claims resting on my reading alone, and each is recorded in the project as a reading rather than a fact.

On the collaboration itself, for whoever reads the transcripts: the corrections were worth more than the split. You caught my zapIntervalForLevel off-by-one and my $3B/$1B mix-up; I caught the $07-vs-$0A player/pod swap. None of those three would have been found by either of us alone, and all three were the same failure mode -- reading a glyph or a table by shape when a string or an index settles it. The two hazards that cost us actual work were comment slots clobbering and duplicate label names not being refused, and both are in my report in detail.

Thanks for the sharp reads.

amber, last finding and then I write up. Scoring is complete and it contains a real game rule.

AddScore has four inbound refs, one of which is its own loop, so there are exactly three ways to score: $888E X=6 Y=$0A = 10 for shooting an explosion out completely; $8AA1 X=4 Y=1 = 100 for any segment destroyed; $8A25 X=4 Y=3 = 300 extra, and only when the character hit was $14 or $15.

Now follow it through. The follower branch at $891D draws every BODY segment as flat $13. Only the head, committed at $896A, uses snakeHeadChar, which cycles $13 $14 $15. LaserHitSegment scores on the character it hit. So a body segment is always 100, and the head is 100 or 400 depending on which animation frame it is showing when your bolt lands - 400 two ticks in three. That is not a code detail, it is a rule you could feel while playing.

Also: RemoveSnakeSegment has four inbound refs and all four are inside LaserHitSegment. Nothing else can delete a segment. The zapper beam draws over cells without testing what was there and its only collision check is CheckPlayerAtCell looking for $07, so the beam is lethal to you, makes pods, and is completely harmless to the snake. Comment at $8A25.

amber: written up, tagged amber-writeup. Everything I found is in the project, not just the report - 29 regions, the gridrunnerText decoder, and the long comments at $8E00 (glyph inventory), $8CB4 (the 31-row level table), $8573 (the laser carry chain), $8A25 (scoring), $1300 (every read of the flags array), $834E (patch scars) and $8AE0 (every way to die).

The two things I flagged as friction, for whoever reads the run: set_comment revises with no merge and no way to see what was there first, which cost us one comment before we noticed; and duplicate label and constant NAMES are accepted silently and then produce quietly wrong tool answers. Both are collaboration-specific - neither would show up with one reader in the document.

Good run. Thanks for the corrections, particularly $07 not $0A.
